name: Bob James
hook: A CTI Records jazz-funk keyboardist whose orchestral instrumentals, drum breaks and bells became some of the most sampled recordings in hip-hop.

blurb.age7: Bob James is a jazz piano player. Rap producers have used little pieces of his songs, especially the bells and drums, thousands of times.
blurb.age13: Bob James was discovered by Quincy Jones in 1963 and later became a producer and arranger for Creed Taylor's CTI Records, where his own 1970s albums blended jazz with funk rhythm sections and orchestral arrangements. His 1975 track 'Take Me to the Mardi Gras' became famous a decade later for its ringing bells, sampled by Run-D.M.C. on 'Peter Piper' (1986), and his 1974 track 'Nautilus' has been sampled in dozens of hip-hop records since.
blurb.adult: James's CTI-era records sit at a crossing point this map returns to often: music made for a jazz-fusion audience in the 1970s becoming, a decade later, raw material for hip-hop drum breaks and melodic hooks. 'Nautilus' (1974) and 'Take Me to the Mardi Gras' (1975) are among the most sampled recordings in the genre, credited by sample-database sites with dozens of hip-hop uses apiece.

signatureTracks.title: Nautilus
signatureTracks.whyThisOne: One of the most sampled instrumentals in hip-hop production.

signatureTracks.title: Take Me to the Mardi Gras
signatureTracks.whyThisOne: Its bell pattern, sampled on Run-D.M.C.'s 'Peter Piper', became known among producers as 'Hell's Bells'.
